items.title: What The Telecom Bust Taught Me About AI’s Debt Boom
items.summary: The AI buildout’s growing reliance on debt echoes the telecom bubble, raising the risk that infrastructure spending will outpace the revenue needed to meet fixed repayment obligations. According to guest author David Spreng of Runway Growth Capital, even if AI fulfills its technological promise, borrowers’ survival will depend on realistic demand forecasts and debt tied to dependable cash flows, with missed timelines potentially forcing restructurings and bankruptcies.

items.title: The Blue Economy: The World’s Quietest Economic Engine And Its Smartest Cities

Alberto Onetti, chairman of Mind the Bridge, writes that ports are emerging as hubs for testing and scaling these technologies, but realizing their potential requires coordination among port authorities, startups, investors and policymakers.

items.title: Public Markets Are Frequently Wrong. The SaaSpocalypse Shows Us Why
items.summary: The “SaaSpocalypse” selloff and uneven recovery exposed public markets’ difficulty distinguishing software companies that benefit from AI from those it threatens, particularly as deeply embedded platforms retain competitive advantages. In this guest essay, Richard Anton, co-founder and general partner of Oxx, argues that this volatility distorts private transaction pricing, undermines confidence in public ownership and makes IPOs less appealing to founders.
